# Jadpo

> An experimental, statically typed programming language for web backends written mainly by LLMs and reviewed by people. The compiler and runtime are written in Rust, with interpreted development and compiled native and WebAssembly deployables.

This is a reading index, not the language specification or a guarantee of automatic retrieval. Follow the linked pages for rules and implementation status. Decided does not mean built. Do not infer the language from the README or a small example alone.

The public project home is https://github.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo. Links to jadpo.dev are the newest docs, and `https://jadpo.dev/v/<version>/` holds the same paths for one release. Links to GitHub track main; use a single checkout or replace main with one commit SHA throughout when a consistent snapshot matters. A URL tool may require every relevant link explicitly. GitHub and the assistant's tools determine access; this file changes no crawler permissions.

## Start here

- [Primer](https://jadpo.dev/docs/primer.md): Read this first before writing an app: layout, syntax, the constructs nearly every app uses, what is built and where to look next; 3,000 to 5,000 tokens, every example compiled.
- [Learn Jadpo](https://jadpo.dev/learn.md): A todo app with sign-in, built a page at a time from an empty folder to a deployed server, for a newcomer; every page's project compiled and tested.
- [Guides](https://jadpo.dev/guides.md): One common job each, start to finish: build an API, store, query, failures, sign-in, outside APIs, background work, tests, approving risky changes, packages and deploying; every guide's project compiled and tested.
- [Agent skill](https://jadpo.dev/.well-known/agent-skills/jadpo/SKILL.md): The skill for a coding agent that writes Jadpo apps: read the primer, find pages, run `jadpo check --json` and `jadpo test --json`, and report a Jadpo bug through the user.
- [Project README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/README.md): Purpose, a compiler error example, status and how to build from source.
- [Examples](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/examples/README.md): Every complete teaching project, with comments and tests, and the closest one for each feature.
- [Vision](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/vision.md): Why Jadpo exists and how responsibility is divided.
- [Roadmap](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/roadmap.md): The only implementation tracker; separates outstanding work from completion.
- [Compiler and runtime](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/compiler-runtime.md): The graph, interpreter, compiled targets and verification architecture.

## Reference

The reference is on the site, one page per topic, in these groups. Open the page of the group a task belongs to, which lists what is in the group. Then fetch only the `.md` pages the task needs.

- [Language](https://jadpo.dev/docs/language.md): How a Jadpo program is laid out and written: its types, logic, failures and standard library.
- [Data](https://jadpo.dev/docs/storing-data.md): What an app stores and how it reads and writes it: entities, migrations, queries, personal data and location.
- [APIs](https://jadpo.dev/docs/apis.md): What an app answers: its routes, who is calling them and what each caller may do.
- [Background work](https://jadpo.dev/docs/jobs-and-events.md): What runs outside a request: schedules, batches, events, and what happens when a delivery fails.
- [Built-in services](https://jadpo.dev/docs/built-in-services.md): What Jadpo gives an app without a package: email, files, flags, rate limits, search, audit, AI and more.
- [External services](https://jadpo.dev/docs/external-services.md): Another company's API from your app: connecting to it, calling it, receiving from it, and using packages.
- [Configuration](https://jadpo.dev/docs/configuration.md): Settings and secrets, and the languages your app speaks: locales and translations.
- [Testing](https://jadpo.dev/docs/testing.md): How your tests run your real application against a real database: kinds of test, fixtures and fakes.
- [Tools](https://jadpo.dev/docs/tooling.md): The jadpo command, your editor, building and deploying, and what a coding agent can look up.

Each compiler error has its own page, `https://jadpo.dev/docs/errors/<rule.id>.md`, such as https://jadpo.dev/docs/errors/failure.kind_required.md, and the error's `help:` line prints its address. Each standard type has one too, such as https://jadpo.dev/docs/types/type-money.md, and `jadpo help <Type>` prints the same page.

## When Jadpo is wrong

If the compiler crashes, rejects code the docs say is valid, accepts code the docs say it refuses, or a page is wrong: check the error's page and the docs first, then cut it down to the smallest project that still shows it. Ask your user before filing anything, because a public issue is published under their name. Give them the drafted report, or a prefilled link to the [bug form](https://github.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/issues/new?template=bug.yml&title=). Include no secrets, settings values or app code beyond that project. After a crash, `~/.cache/jadpo/crashes/` holds a file for the report; your user reads it before it is attached. Never post on your own. A suspected security hole goes to the private route in [SECURITY.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/SECURITY.md), never a public issue.

## Contributing to the compiler

- [Language map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/language/README.md): The whole area pages and their design notes, for changing the language. One can be over 100,000 tokens; to write an app, use the topics above.
- [Contributor guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): Build prerequisites, verification and contribution workflow.
- [Repository instructions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/AGENTS.md): Working rules for changes to this compiler repository.
- [Documentation index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/README.md): Architecture, decisions and design context.
- [Benchmarks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/benchmarks/README.md): The golden todo, its TypeScript twin and contract cases, and the harnesses that measure Jadpo against TypeScript.
- [CLI design language](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jadpo-dev/jadpo/main/docs/cli-design-language.md): How everything `jadpo` prints, and every generated page, looks and behaves.
